scope: Triage of one strict OASIS trace report. Families explain non-passing cases; they never change a case status or total, never suppress a mismatch and grant no conformance credit. Trace classification does not show that the normative clauses are covered; the full requirement-to-test ledger remains open.
classification_rule: Each case belongs to exactly one family. The family is matched by case key, status, strict failed exchange and the strict detail. Its classification describes the governing blocker: the earliest known mismatch that no cited normative text permits, from the strict report, the official diagnostic mode or research probes. If every known mismatch is a permitted variation, the classification is permitted_reference_choice.

classifications.missing_server_feature: Behaviour the server does not implement.
classifications.server_defect: Implemented behaviour that contradicts normative text.
classifications.permitted_reference_choice: The trace shows one reference-server choice and cited normative text permits the server to differ.
classifications.fixture_corpus_or_harness: Trace corpus defect or gap, or a harness limitation.
classifications.dependency_determinism_interop: The case needs cross-case state, deterministic or variable-output handling, or Interop wrapper handling.
classifications.unresolved_spec_ambiguity: Normative text supports more than one reading; no TC interpretation is cited.

provenance.triaged_report: OASIS qualification report (development record, not committed)
provenance.scope: Re-triage: all 439 case records compared with the previous triage. Only TL-M-2-30 changes to passed; three existing randomized ciphertext details vary. No independent replay or review is claimed.
provenance.runtime_source_note: 64 runtime sources match the integrated candidate and copied tested native binary; the earlier triage fixes, legacy destroyed Get and Alternative Name changes are included.
provenance.previous_identity: The previous triage (strict 147 passed, 126 failed, 166 unexecuted) is kept in the development records.
